stories.label: Trump administration wants Ukraine and Russia to reach peace deal by January 2027
stories.summary: After Berlin talks with Zelensky and the Coalition of the Willing, envoy Jared Kushner says Moscow appears ready to accept NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine, and Washington wants a deal by January 2027. Lead with the guarantee claim and the deadline; explain what a guarantee short of NATO membership means, who would enforce it, and what Ukraine is being asked to give up. Ukrainska Pravda carries Kyiv's reading. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: Spanish PM Sanchez admits to 'mistakes' 10 days before elections
stories.summary: In the only televised debate before Spain's election, Pedro Sánchez conceded 'mistakes' as Alberto Núñez Feijóo hit him on corruption cases and housing. Lead with the admission and the two issues that decide the vote; explain what is at stake: whether the PP needs Vox to govern, and what that means for one of Europe's few governments that recognised Palestine. Anadolu and the Express Tribune give the non-European read. Dateline Madrid.

stories.label: Estonia to Close Russian Border as Moscow Threatens Response
stories.summary: Estonia will shut every land crossing with Russia on 1 December for at least six months, and Moscow's foreign ministry promises a response. Lead with the closure date and who it strands: Narva's Russian-speaking residents and families split across the river. Explain why Tallinn is doing it now, the same day Poland reports three Russian objects in its airspace, and treat Moscow's warning as TASS reports it. Dateline Tallinn.

stories.label: Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Strait of Hormuz - UKMTO
stories.summary: New since our 19 November LNG story: a tanker caught fire after a projectile hit it 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, by UKMTO's account, while Iran moves crude ship-to-ship to test the US blockade (Al-Monitor). Lead with the strike. The surprise is that Brent crude is still heading for a third weekly loss, below $91, because returning Gulf supply outweighs the war risk. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude as the series. Dateline Khasab.

stories.label: Sudan’s Power Grid on Brink of Collapse Following Wave of Strikes Targeting Electricity Stations
stories.summary: A wave of drone strikes on Sudan's power stations has left the national grid near collapse: hospitals are running without power, farms cannot pump water, and repair is not in sight. Lead with what has gone dark and who pays: civilians in army-held cities. Name who is hitting the stations and why infrastructure has become the target in the SAF–RSF war. This is the Sudan coverage the daily audit says is missing. Dateline Port Sudan unless the report places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Houthis say they attacked power plant, port in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The Houthis' spokesman Yahya Saree claims strikes on a Saudi power plant and port, as retaliation for coalition strikes on power plants in Saada and Mokha and the shelling of a Hodeidah port berth. Lead with the tit-for-tat on power infrastructure, which the cost of the war has now reached on both sides of the border. The only source is Russian state agency TASS relaying a Houthi claim: attribute every claim and state nothing as fact. Dateline Sanaa.

stories.label: Protests held across Europe over wages, services, high living costs
stories.summary: Workers and students rallied in 25 European countries, on the model of France's protests, against high living costs, stagnant wages and military spending crowding out public services. Italy's CGIL is out in Rome. Lead with how far the protests have spread and the trade-off they name: governments raising defence budgets while wages and services fall behind. Dateline Rome.

stories.label: Live news: Bitcoin hovers just above $61,000 as Anthropic slides 13% after Nasdaq debut
stories.summary: The US AI selloff has spread to Asia: South Korea's Kospi fell more than 5%, the market that holds Samsung and SK Hynix, while Anthropic is down 13% from its Nasdaq debut. Lead with the Kospi drop and the memory-chip names; this is the move behind Samsung's 11% and TSMC's 15% weekly falls. Explain the mechanism, doubt about AI capex flowing back to the chipmakers, and leave bitcoin as a secondary line since our ETF-outflow story already reported it. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Valve says it might have to raise the price of supply-limited Steam Machines
stories.summary: Valve says it may raise the Steam Machine's price again because it still cannot buy RAM and storage at a reasonable cost. Lead with the mechanism: the AI data-centre build-out has absorbed the memory supply, and the cost now lands on consumer hardware. Tie it to the memory makers (Micron, Samsung) whose shares fell this week, and show how a shortage priced for hyperscalers reaches an ordinary buyer.

stories.label: Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university
stories.summary: Amazon researchers say a China-linked group used Cairn, an open-source AI penetration-testing tool, to keep attacking two universities, and in one case it may have found a zero-day on its own. Lead with the possible AI-found zero-day. That is the threshold security people have been waiting for: offensive AI that no longer needs a skilled operator. Attribute the attribution to Amazon.

stories.label: Tencent releases Hy4 model weights with million-token context
stories.summary: Tencent has released the weights of its flagship Hy4 model under Apache 2.0, with a million-token context and text, image and video understanding, so anyone can download it, deploy it and build on it commercially. Lead with the licence. China's largest labs keep giving away frontier-class weights while US labs close theirs, and this is how Chinese models win developers worldwide. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: Kids Act: EU-Datenschutzbehörde warnt vor Alterskontrollen
stories.summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor calls the Commission's planned online age checks in the Kids Act unnecessary and immature, and lists ten objections. Lead with the EU's own privacy watchdog opposing the Commission. The mechanism: verifying age means identifying every user, adults included, to protect children. Pick the two or three objections with the most consequence. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: German attack drones pass live-fire tests, with first deliveries planned this year
stories.summary: Germany's procurement office says two one-way attack drone variants, including Helsing's HX-2, passed live-fire trials, and deliveries and troop training will start before year end. Lead with Germany fielding loitering munitions of the kind Ukraine's war made standard. Explain who builds them, what software-defined targeting means, and how fast Berlin moved from hesitancy to buying them. Dateline Koblenz.

stories.label: Spiders, beetles and one garage alligator: Largest study to date reveals wildlife sharing our indoor spaces
stories.summary: The largest survey yet of life inside homes catalogues more than 2,000 species in over 20,000 records from the US and Canada. Lead with the scale: the house is an ecosystem. Explain what the database lets scientists study, such as pest spread, allergens and the species that now live only indoors, and name the journal.

stories.label: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkiye
stories.summary: Malaysia, which hosts some of the largest Rohingya population outside Bangladesh without recognising them as refugees, will move 10,000 to Turkey through a skills-training scheme: one of the biggest Rohingya resettlements since the 2017 Rakhine crackdown. Lead with the number and the mechanism (labour-skills channel rather than refugee status), and why two Muslim-majority states are doing what Western resettlement programmes have not. Follow-up context: it comes days after the ICJ found Myanmar forces killed some 10,000 Rohingya; dateline Kuala Lumpur.

stories.label: El Salvador's Bukele to run for third presidential term
stories.summary: Bukele registered with the Supreme Electoral Court for a third term, which the constitution once barred outright; lead with the registration itself and the 'six more years' crowd. The mechanism: a loyalist legislature and a court he reshaped removed the term limits, and the state of exception that jailed tens of thousands keeps his approval high. Who bears the cost: detainees held without trial and an opposition with no institutional check left. Dateline San Salvador.

stories.label: French Ex-PM Villepin Announces Presidential Run
stories.summary: Dominique de Villepin, the prime minister remembered for France's 2003 UN stand against the Iraq invasion and a vocal critic of the war on Gaza, enters the 2027 race decrying a 'decaying' France. Lead with what his candidacy puts on the ballot: a Gaullist foreign-policy line in a field where the far right leads and the centre has fragmented. Asharq Al-Awsat carries the regional view. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Afghanistan not invited to ECO moot as Islamabad does not recognise Kabul regime: FO
stories.summary: Pakistan, hosting the Economic Cooperation Organisation's foreign ministers in Islamabad, left Afghanistan off the invitation list because it does not recognise the Taliban government, shutting a founding regional member out of a trade and connectivity bloc. Lead with the exclusion and the stated reason; the mechanism is that Pakistan-Taliban relations have broken down over cross-border militant attacks and closed crossings, and Afghan traders and transit routes bear the cost. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $582M in a Day as BTC Drops Below $62K
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $62,000, down 10% in a week, as BlackRock's bitcoin fund posted a record outflow and spot ETFs shed $582 million in a day. The cause is the point: bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike and a US tech sell-off that spread to Asia, the same move behind the week's fall in TSMC, Samsung and Micron. Lead with the record outflow, then the mechanism: the ETFs that tied bitcoin to Wall Street now carry the Fed's rate path straight into it. Chart: bitcoin.

stories.label: Short-term inflation reaches 10.41pc on costly flour
stories.summary: Pakistan's weekly price index rose 10.41% year on year, driven by wheat flour. Lead with flour: the staple of the poorest households, whose cost lands hardest on them. Mechanism: a poor regional wheat crop (India's sowing fell the most in 26 years) and fuel costs feeding through. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Bank of Russia's gold reserves decrease by 0.3 million troy ounces
stories.summary: The Bank of Russia's gold holdings fell to 72.5 million troy ounces in October, the lowest since October 2019, according to central bank data reported by Russian state news agency TASS (attribute it so). Mechanism: with Western sanctions freezing its foreign-currency reserves, gold is the reserve Moscow can actually spend, and the National Wealth Fund has been selling it to cover a war-swollen budget deficit. Chart: gold. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Astronomers reveal the oceanic origin of Europa's sodium cloud
stories.summary: Two decades of Keck Observatory measurements show the sodium cloud around Jupiter's moon Europa has stayed strikingly stable despite Jupiter's violent environment, which points to a steady source: salt from the ocean under the ice. Lead with the 20-year stability and why it implicates the ocean rather than Io's volcanoes; what's next is NASA's Europa Clipper, arriving 2030, which can test it. Dateline Maunakea, Hawaii.

stories.label: US science academy urges journals to fix errors more quickly
stories.summary: A National Academies report finds journals take too long to retract or correct flawed papers and apply inconsistent standards, and that nobody even collects data on how long it takes. Lead with that missing number. Mechanism: publishers have little incentive to retract, so flawed results keep being cited and built on, in medicine as elsewhere. Name the recommendations and who must act on them. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: BTC news: Bitcoin wallet mistakes exposed $106 million to thieves, researchers find
stories.summary: Researchers found wallet software reusing or mis-generating the signature nonce, an old cryptographic mistake that lets anyone compute the private key from the blockchain; vulnerable addresses held up to about $106 million. When the researchers exposed keys of their own as bait, bots drained them within seconds. Lead with the seconds-long sweep; the mechanism is one bad random number in a signature; be precise that how much was actually stolen is not established.

stories.label: Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US
stories.summary: TP-Link, likely the top supplier of routers to US homes and small businesses, still cannot sell its newest Wi-Fi models in the US under the administration's sweeping ban on foreign-made communications equipment. Lead with the market share frozen out; the mechanism is equipment authorisation at the FCC used as a gate, and the cost falls on buyers left with older, less secure hardware. Name what the company has done to comply and what the government asks in return.

stories.label: AI时代，华为要再造一个“荣耀”！首款鸿蒙AI手机来了
stories.summary: Huawei launched OSTA, its first new phone sub-brand since it was forced to sell Honor in 2020, with the OSTA O1 Pro on its own Kirin 9030S chip and HarmonyOS 7: an agent-style assistant that books restaurants, sends WeChat messages and hails Didi from one spoken command, at 5,499 yuan. Lead with the comeback: six years after US sanctions cost it Honor, Huawei has rebuilt chips and an operating system at home and is splitting into two brands again. Inside view from mainland tech press. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: Poland investigates possible airspace violations near Ukraine border
stories.summary: A suspected Russian cruise missile came down and burned in a field in Lublin province, 28 miles inside Poland and about 60 miles from where Coalition of the Willing troops, British among them, were exercising. Lead with the distance from the troops: a NATO state's airspace was crossed during a Russian strike on Ukraine, and the question is what Warsaw and the alliance do when the debris lands this close to foreign soldiers. Note Moscow's same-day line, via TASS, that NATO is 'openly preparing' for war.

stories.label: Pakistan minister visits India for first time since 2025 war
stories.summary: Pakistani minister Musadik Malik is in New Delhi for an SCO Civilisation Dialogue — the first ministerial visit since the May 2025 war — and India's opposition Congress is attacking the government for inviting him. Lead with the multilateral cover: the SCO forces a contact neither capital would arrange bilaterally. Set the Indian domestic backlash (Pahalgam) against how Dawn and Pakistani outlets frame the visit; what talks, if any, happen on the sidelines.

stories.label: Lufthansa to Eliminate 1,000 Jobs At Struggling Flagship Airline
stories.summary: Lufthansa will cut 1,000 full-time jobs at its loss-making mainline airline at the Munich and Frankfurt hubs, with high jet fuel costs named as the pressure. Lead with the cost chain: the Iran war's grip on Gulf energy shows up as job losses at Europe's largest airline group. Name Brent crude as the series behind the fuel bill, and note the collective-bargaining fight with pilots and cabin unions that follows.

stories.label: India's wheat area set for biggest drop in 26 years as farmers switch crops
stories.summary: India's wheat acreage is heading for its steepest fall in 26 years because the weakest monsoon in over a decade left fields parched and farmers are switching to chickpeas and other crops that pay better on less water. Lead with the 26-year figure. The world's second-largest wheat producer planting less raises the odds of imports and food inflation for hundreds of millions; name wheat prices as the series and El Niño as the driver.

stories.label: Oil loses grip on bond markets as inflation 'virus' spreads
stories.summary: All year, government borrowing costs tracked Brent crude because the Iran war's energy shock was the inflation story; that link has now broken, as traders price how central banks handle inflation that has spread from fuel into the wider economy. Lead with the mechanism: when inflation stops depending on oil, a ceasefire or a price drop no longer brings yields down. Name Brent crude and the US 10-year Treasury yield as the series, and who pays — governments and borrowers refinancing at higher rates.

stories.label: Lula visits ailing Chief Raoni as Brazil recognises Indigenous land
stories.summary: Brazil declared Kapot Nhinore in Mato Grosso the permanent land of the Mebengokre (Kayapó) and Yudja peoples, a legal step toward demarcation, as Lula visited the ailing Chief Raoni. Lead with the land, not the visit: who held the claim, how long it waited, and which ranching or soy interests contest it in the agribusiness heartland. Explain what the declaration protects and what demarcation still requires.

stories.label: Israeli Diplomat Offered Iowa Attorney General Free Trip, Then Asked for Favors
stories.summary: FOIA records and hacked email archives show an Israeli diplomat offered Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird a free trip and then asked her for favours, including support for laws against boycotts of Israel. Lead with the sequence — gift, then ask — documented in the state's own records. The mechanism is the pattern: Israel cultivating state-level officials to pass anti-boycott laws that restrict Americans' speech, below the federal scrutiny of foreign lobbying.

stories.label: Deep Dive: The Pentagon Fails Ninth Consecutive Annual Audit
stories.summary: The Pentagon failed its ninth straight annual audit: the Inspector General's auditors could not gather enough evidence to say whether its numbers are correct. Lead with that — the largest US agency, now funding a war with Iran, cannot show where its money goes. Give the budget size, the share of assets that cannot be accounted for, and the 2028 clean-audit deadline Congress set.

stories.label: Waymo被迫退出高速公路，无人驾驶的商业化开始碰到监管天花板
stories.summary: Waymo has been forced off highways, and the Chinese tech press reads it as robotaxi commercialisation hitting a regulatory ceiling. Lead with what made Waymo withdraw and which regulator acted. The structural point, from a mainland view: whether a car can drive like a human is no longer the question — who permits it at speed is, and Chinese rivals Baidu Apollo and Pony.ai face the same ceiling.

stories.label: Danish Soldiers Are Sneaking Starlink Terminals into Greenland
stories.summary: A parliamentary question from Greenlandic politician Pele Broberg says Danish soldiers are bringing privately owned Starlink terminals into Greenland despite restrictions. Lead with the contradiction: the same week Denmark ratified its security deal with Washington, its own troops route around rules on Elon Musk's satellite network. The mechanism is sovereignty over communications — Europe has no alternative to Starlink in the Arctic, and IRIS² is years off.

stories.label: NCCIA arrests suspect over alleged sale of stolen US government data in Karachi
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency arrested a Karachi suspect accused of acquiring and selling confidential data from US government agencies, law enforcement and private companies. Lead with what was sold and to whom — which agencies' data, through which marketplace. Pakistan acting on breaches of US systems shows the cross-border data trade and the cooperation behind the arrest.

stories.label: Galactic shock: Discovery challenges our understanding of the Milky Way's structure
stories.summary: A University of Sydney PhD student found that the Milky Way is unusual in where it forms new stars compared with nearby galaxies. Lead with the finding: our galaxy, used as the template for galaxy models, may be an outlier. Explain how star formation was measured across the comparison galaxies and what it means for models that assume the Milky Way is typical.

stories.label: Fed's Goolsbee Says All Options on FOMC Table Amid Hot Inflation
stories.summary: After several hot US inflation prints, Chicago Fed president Goolsbee will not rule out a larger-than-usual rate rise in December, and he names the AI investment surge as a source of overheating. Lead with the Fed rate and the US 10-year Treasury yield. Then follow who pays abroad: the Mexican peso fell past 19 per dollar, its weakest in 17 months (Bloomberg), and bitcoin traders are hedging against a hike. Dateline: Washington.

stories.label: US let Nvidia and AMD sell bucketloads of chips to military-linked Chinese companies
stories.summary: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security licensed hundreds of thousands of advanced Nvidia and AMD GPUs to firms the Department of War itself lists as Chinese military companies. Lead with that contradiction: one arm of Washington blacklists the buyers, another licenses the sales. Note that few chips actually shipped and Chinese clouds have moved on to domestic silicon, so the export regime constrained neither side. AMD shares are down 16% in a week; say only what the source supports about why.

stories.label: Cyberattack targets JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard
stories.summary: Hackers took customer data belonging to JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard through a shared third-party vendor, days after JPMorgan's own outage. Lead with the mechanism: three pillars of the payment system share one contractor, so one breach hits all three. Who holds the risk is the customer, whose data was taken although the banks say nothing 'sensitive' was.

stories.label: White House Dismisses Trump's Cyber Security Chief Cairncross
stories.summary: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is out after a run of technical failures across US systems, the week the JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard breach landed. Lead with the timing and the accountability question: the post that coordinates federal cyber defence is now empty while the outages continue. Use DW and TRT for how it reads abroad.

stories.label: South Africa Hawkishly Holds Rates as Inflation Risks Widen
stories.summary: The South African Reserve Bank under Lesetja Kganyago held the repo rate but warned it is ready to hike as inflation risks widen. Lead with the decision and what drives the risk (fuel, a firm dollar, a possible Fed hike). Who pays: South African borrowers already carrying high real rates, while clinics in Cape Town report medicine shortages.

stories.label: Japan's core inflation accelerates in October, cementing rate hike expectations
stories.summary: Japan's core consumer prices rose 2.2% in October, cementing a Bank of Japan rate hike next month. Lead with the data, then the mechanism Reuters reports: board members agree on December but split on how far rates should go, and that ambiguity invites fresh selling of the yen, near 159 per dollar and close to the level where Tokyo has intervened. Name the yen as the series.

stories.label: Xi meets Indonesian president in Shenzhen
stories.summary: This is not the trilateral, which was covered. It is Indonesia's own track: Prabowo Subianto met Xi Jinping on the APEC sidelines. Lead with what the largest Muslim-majority country asked for and got (trade, nickel and investment, the South China Sea), and how Jakarta positions itself between Washington and Beijing after Shenzhen. Use Antara and Tempo for Jakarta's account and attribute China Daily's.

stories.label: Pakistan among 15 nations that welcome UK, Australia sanctions on Israeli settlements, hope others follow suit
stories.summary: Fifteen states, including Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt and Jordan, jointly welcomed British and Australian sanctions on Israeli settlement activity in the occupied West Bank and called on others to follow. Lead with the sanctions themselves (who and what they target) and the fact that two close Western allies of Israel acted. The structural point: settlement expansion is illegal under international law, and these are among the few measures with a cost attached.

stories.label: Lahore once again ranks as world's most polluted major city as AQI crosses 400
stories.summary: Smog pushed Lahore's hourly AQI to 465, and Gujranwala and Multan to 661 and 641, far into the hazardous band. Lead with those numbers and who breathes them: tens of millions in Punjab, children and outdoor workers first. The mechanism is brick kilns, crop burning and traffic in a winter inversion that returns every year, and the accountability question is why each season's measures fail.

stories.label: ETH news: Ethereum's next big upgrade is pushed into 2027 by apps it would break
stories.summary: Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade slips from December to late January at the earliest, because deployed smart contracts would break under it. Lead with the mechanism: immutable code means a protocol change can strand the applications built on it, so core developers wait for companies to patch. That is a governance lesson for any platform whose users cannot be forced to upgrade.

stories.label: Armed violence surges in Colombia despite De la Espriella security push
stories.summary: Armed violence is rising in Colombia even as President De la Espriella's government bombs and launches ground offensives against armed groups. Lead with the toll and the regions hit, and who bears it: rural and Indigenous communities caught between the groups and the strikes. The mechanism: a military-first policy fragments the groups without taking away the coca and mining economies that fund them.

stories.label: Iowans Brace For Lead Dust Cloud As Army Plans To Detonate Unstable Chemicals
stories.summary: On Friday the US Army will blow up nearly five tons of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, and lead-bearing particles could reach communities up to 100 miles away. Lead with the five tons and the 100 miles. The accountability question is who decided open detonation was acceptable, what the EPA required, and what residents were told to do. Dateline: Middletown, Iowa.

stories.label: 'Joanne Young verdict must mark turning point in violence against women'
stories.summary: Philip Young was convicted of drugging his then-wife, Joanne Young, and recruiting strangers online to rape her while she was unconscious. It is Britain's echo of the Pelicot case in France. Lead with the verdict and with how she found out. The structural point is that drug-facilitated abuse inside marriage stays hidden until someone films it, and campaigners (Refuge) want the case to change how police and courts treat it. Dateline: Winchester.

stories.label: Masacre de 12 personas en el norte de Honduras deja a defensora del territorio y su familia asesinada
stories.summary: Delma Yolanda Olvera, the first woman to lead the Tolupán tribe of Mina Honda, helped win Yorito its status as a mining-free municipality in 2019. She was killed with her daughter and husband in Pacayal, in a wave of armed attacks that left 12 dead in the municipality. Lead with who she was and the 12 dead. The mechanism is that land defenders in Honduras are killed while the state answers by declaring a 'high-risk zone' rather than prosecuting anyone. Dateline: Yorito.

stories.label: Silicon Valley elites 'bankrolled' news platform Visegrad24 publishing pro-Israel content: report
stories.summary: A Wired investigation, reported by Dawn, traces how Visegrad24, the Polish-run X account that grew into an anti-migrant, pro-Israel outlet, was bankrolled by Silicon Valley money. Lead with who funded it. The mechanism is that private tech wealth buys reach for a feed that presents itself as neutral news, and readers in the Muslim world meet its framing of Gaza on their timelines. Dateline: Warsaw.

stories.label: NCCIA claims uncovering network allegedly involved in 'up to Rs1tr' betting, money laundering
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency says it has uncovered an online betting and money-laundering network with up to Rs1 trillion in transaction exposure. Lead with the size against Pakistan's economy, and with how money moved through bank accounts and front businesses under the State Bank's watch. Present it as the agency's claim, not a proven figure. Dateline: Karachi.

stories.label: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
stories.summary: Four Black students held at gunpoint by police because an AI camera read a Doritos bag as a gun are now suing their school system and the police. The lawsuit says more than 99% of the system's AI gun alerts were false positives. Lead with the 99%. The mechanism is a vendor's alert reaching armed officers with no human check in between, and the cost of every false positive falling on Black teenagers. Dateline: Baltimore.

stories.label: ARTEX Didn’t Invent New Attacks. It Ended Our Grace Period.
stories.summary: On November 13 the FBI issued a flash alert on ARTEX, an AI-powered hacking tool. SMEX, the Beirut digital-rights group, explains what it means for journalists and NGOs across the Arab region. ARTEX automates known attacks rather than inventing new ones, so the organisations that relied on attackers being too slow to exploit unpatched systems have lost that margin. Lead with that 'grace period', and with which civil-society groups are most exposed. Dateline: Beirut.

stories.label: Worsening medicine shortages leave Cape Town's neglected patients waiting in desperation
stories.summary: Epilepsy medication and cancer drugs are running out at South Africa's public clinics, and the poorest patients, who cannot buy privately, queue from dawn and go home without them. Lead with a named drug that is missing and what happens to a patient who misses doses. The mechanism is the supply-chain and tender failures behind the shortage, and who in the health department answers for them. Dateline: Cape Town.

stories.label: Impacts Of Latest Neptune Missile Strike On Kerch Bridge Seen In Satellite Imagery
stories.summary: Satellite imagery shows the damage from Ukraine's latest Neptune missile strike on the Kerch Bridge, and shows the rail span holding up better than the road span did. Lead with what the imagery shows. The stakes are that the rail line is Russia's main land supply route into occupied Crimea, and the strike came days after the Shenzhen summit left the war unmentioned. Dateline: Kerch.

stories.label: Quase todas as cidades já sofrem com eventos extremos. O que farão os prefeitos?
stories.summary: Agência Pública reports that almost every Brazilian municipality has already suffered extreme weather, and that heat alone could kill 13,000 Brazilians this summer. Lead with the 13,000. The accountability point is that adaptation (shade, cooling, drainage, early warning) is the job of mayors, and most cities have no plan ahead of the municipal elections. Dateline: São Paulo.

stories.label: Ethiopian volcano's mysterious methane outburst may have a culprit—magma that never erupted
stories.summary: Satellites caught an Ethiopian volcano releasing huge amounts of methane without erupting. A University of Bristol-led team traces the gas to magma that rose and stalled underground, heating organic-rich sediments. Lead with the puzzle and the answer. The wider stake is that underground magma could have driven methane pulses in Earth's past climate, which changes how past warming events are read. Dateline: Bristol.

stories.label: Who is getting rich from Anthropic's record IPO
stories.summary: New since the $83 pricing we covered: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq as ANT at $111.50, up about 34%, a market value near $1.45 trillion after raising about $81bn, the largest IPO on record. Lead with who holds the power: seven founders own about 12.7% of the shares but control about 61% of the votes through a single Class F share, and each Amodei sibling's stake is worth about $26bn. The mechanism is the prospectus: about $900bn in compute purchase and lease commitments, many take-or-pay, against a junk-grade credit rating, with Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC (suppliers and customers) buying $26bn of non-voting stock. Polymarket's odds of a $1.25-1.50T valuation fell from 45% to 15% this week before the debut. Dateline New York.

stories.label: EU Executive Branch Suffered AI-Driven Cyber-Attack in October
stories.summary: The European Commission confirmed that attackers misused an AI tool to break into its systems in late October, and that it shut systems down to contain the intrusion; it disclosed this only now, weeks later. Lead with the admission and the delay: the body writing the EU's AI Act and its cyber rules is among the first governments to say an AI-assisted attack hit it. Say what is known about whose data was exposed and what the AI tool did, and keep what is unknown out of the facts. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: LNG transportation in Hormuz dropped to minimum amid new attacks -- Bloomberg
stories.summary: Only two LNG carriers crossed the Strait of Hormuz in the week to 17 November, as renewed attacks on shipping drove gas transits back to their minimum. The figure comes from Bloomberg tanker tracking reported by Russian state news agency TASS; attribute it so, and do not state the count as fact. Who pays: Qatar, the world's richest LNG exporter, whose economy the IMF expects to shrink more than 14% this year, and the Asian buyers who rely on its gas. Polymarket's odds of an effective US-Iran ceasefire by 22 November fell from 63% to 35% this week. Chart natural gas and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Doha.

stories.label: Egypt reaches staff-level deal for $2.3bn in IMF funding
stories.summary: Egypt has reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF that unlocks $2.3bn. Lead with what the money is conditional on (subsidy cuts, asset sales, the state and army's share of the economy) and who bears it: Egyptian households already paying for a weak pound and an Iran war that has cut Suez Canal revenue. Our 15 November story on the Red Sea land decree for public debt is the context. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Digital levy: While Germany waits, big tech’s tax gap grows
stories.summary: A new study puts big tech's tax gap (record profits taxed at ever lower rates) near €300bn. Germany is Europe's largest market without a digital levy, and the culture minister's promised key-points paper has not appeared a year later. Lead with the €300bn and the mechanism, profit booked where tax is lowest, then name who keeps the government from acting. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: COP31: Civil Society groups fault omitting fossil fuel phase-out from draft text
stories.summary: New since our 16 November story on the draft cover decision: the latest COP31 text, published less than 48 hours before the talks close, drops any language on transitioning away from fossil fuels and so steps back from the Dubai agreement. Lead with what was deleted and who pushed for it; 350.org and others name the producers. The cost falls on the countries already paying in floods and heat. Dateline Antalya.

stories.label: PL Samuel Klein é aprovado no Senado e vai à sanção presidencial
stories.summary: Brazil's Senate passed the 'Samuel Klein bill', which extends from 3 to 20 years the time victims of childhood sexual abuse have to sue their abusers, and sent it to the president to sign. The bill is named after the late Casas Bahia founder, whose alleged abuse Agência Pública's own reporting exposed and who could not be sued because the time limit had expired. Lead with the 3-to-20-year change and the reporting behind it. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Félix Gallardo’s Death Leaves Mexico’s Corruption Story Unfinished
stories.summary: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, founder of the Guadalajara Cartel, has died after 37 years in prison, and the officials, police and politicians who protected his trade were never prosecuted. Lead with the death; the mechanism is the state protection his network relied on, a pattern InSight Crime traces into Mexico's corruption today. Keep it news: what he built, who shielded him, and what went unanswered. Dateline Guadalajara.

stories.label: Huge extinct orca may have eaten other whales | New Scientist
stories.summary: Fossils show a nearly 8-metre orca species that lived in the North Sea more than 2 million years ago, and suggest orcas began hunting marine mammals much earlier than thought. Lead with the size and the date; the finding is that the ocean's top predator held that role for far longer than believed. Say how the diet was inferred, from teeth or from wear, and how strong that evidence is.

stories.label: ESA Awards OHB €102M Contract for ClearSpace-1 Debris Removal Mission
stories.summary: ESA has signed a €102m contract with Germany's OHB to build ClearSpace-1, which will capture and deorbit ESA's own retired Proba-1 satellite, moving the debris-removal mission from study to construction. Lead with the mechanism: capturing an object never built to be caught, the hard problem in clearing orbit. Mention that the mission's target changed after an earlier one was hit by debris. Dateline Bremen.

stories.label: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
stories.summary: From January 2027, Android phones worldwide will refuse to install apps from developers who have not registered their identity with Google, even apps from outside the Play Store. Google first enforced this in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. Lead with the reach: one company becomes the gatekeeper for software on roughly three billion devices it does not sell. Name who loses: anonymous and open-source developers, F-Droid, and activists who sideload tools. Dateline Mountain View.

stories.label: Black Neighborhoods Are Twice as Likely To House a Data Center, Study Finds
stories.summary: A study finds US data centres are twice as likely to sit in majority-Black neighbourhoods, 2.6 times in majority-Hispanic and 4.2 times in majority-Asian ones, and ties the pattern to redlining. Lead with the ratios; the mechanism is cheap industrial land and weak zoning in neighbourhoods drawn by old segregation maps, and those residents absorb the noise, water use and gas turbines. xAI's Memphis site is the known case. Say who did the study and how.

stories.label: Vermutlich illegal: Bundespolizei soll Online-Werbung für Überwachung nutzen
stories.summary: Germany's federal police reportedly use a surveillance tool built on online advertising data (the location pings apps sell to ad exchanges) that can follow millions of phones step by step, with no clear legal basis. Bloomberg reported it first and netzpolitik.org assesses the legality; Die Linke in the Bundestag calls it a scandal. Lead with the mechanism: police buy the data instead of seeking a warrant. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: AI isn’t replacing your job. It’s turning it into low-paid gig work
stories.summary: AI training platforms recruit doctors, lawyers and PhDs at top rates to teach their models, then cut pay and drop workers without notice, the same tactics long used on data labellers in Kenya and the Philippines. Lead with a named worker and the drop in pay. The mechanism: expert labour is being turned into gig work to train the systems meant to replace it. Dateline where the workers are, not Silicon Valley.
